data.narrative:
Interlune is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Rob Meyerson, Gary Lai, and Harrison Schmitt, having raised $23M to date. The sector peer universe comprises 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs.

Valuation triangulation proved limited by data constraints. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist in Space & Aerospace, none satisfy the filters required for a credible narrow peer set (zero companies at identical or adjacent stage with comparable valuation tier). Public-comp anchoring anchors to a sector P/S median of 27.4x across the 6 public tickers, but cannot be applied because Interlune's revenue is not on file—a typical constraint for early-stage private companies. Standard venture-stage methods (DCF, comparable transaction multiples on revenue or EBITDA) lack sufficient input data.

Without applicable quantitative anchors, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range. The raised capital of $23M establishes a floor only insofar as it reflects past investor conviction, but provides no forward valuation estimate. Resolution would require either (1) disclosure of Interlune's projected revenue or near-term financial metrics, (2) identification of transaction precedents in lunar technology or in-situ resource utilization, or (3) completion of a seed post-money valuation from the most recent financing round.
